answer.with_labelled_history: Bayesian aggregation (BMA) or BLP / calibration-weighted linear pooling, not equal-weight linear or equal-weight log pooling.

call_sheet_grade.claim: calibration-weighted aggregation blocked on a labelled history

canonical_mechanism: With labelled verdict history, Bayesian aggregation (BMA) or a recalibrated/weighted linear pool is the better-calibrated family when members differ in calibration. This program does not have that history, so those operators are blocked. The method usable TODAY at zero history is equal-weight linear pooling.

claims.canonical_mechanism: Equal-weight linear pooling is defined from the current member probabilities alone and is therefore usable at zero labelled history.

claims.strongest_caveat: Usable does not mean well calibrated: Ranjan and Gneiting (2010) Section 2 prove any non-trivial linear pool of distinct calibrated binary forecasts is itself uncalibrated.

claims.canonical_mechanism: When members are calibrated, a linear pool is nevertheless miscalibrated (underconfident). Recalibrated linear pooling (BLP) cuts Brier score relative to equal-weight and optimally weighted linear pools, but BLP parameters are fit on labelled training outcomes.

claims.canonical_mechanism: Logarithmic / log-linear pooling is defined at zero history (equal weights) and, when weights are estimated by maximum likelihood on labelled data, can match the true conditional on independent sources. Equal-weight log pooling is not the same operator as ML log-linear pooling.

claims.strongest_caveat: Table 4's winning log-linear row uses ML weights (1.46), i.e. labelled data. Equal-weight log pooling also 0-forces: one member at 0 or 1 vetoes the pool. This program's live unequal-calibration control (seed 79) gives equal-weight log Brier 0.224907 and ECE 0.098636 versus equal-weight linear Brier 0.209190 and ECE 0.033567; log pooling is worse on both scores in that DGP.

claims.canonical_mechanism: Bayesian model averaging produces better calibrated predictive distributions than a raw ensemble by setting member weights to posterior model probabilities estimated on a labelled training window. With a uniform prior and empty history the posterior equals the prior and BMA collapses to equal-weight linear pooling of the component densities.

claims.strongest_caveat: The 25-day labelled window is the prerequisite this program does not have. Empty-history BMA is not a third operator; it is equal-weight linear pooling under another name.

evidence_tier_policy: E1 verbatim primary table/theorem; E2 independent multi-source; E3 single source or headline without baseline - cannot promote; E4 degraded-fetch / inferred. A headline number without its baseline is E3 and cannot promote a mechanism.

live_control.note: BMA posterior on this DGP concentrates on the calibrated member (weight ~1), which is the correct unequal-calibration behaviour. ECE is the calibration-relevant score; Brier also does not get worse.

method_table.calibration_when_members_differ: Defined. Robust to a 0/1 veto. Theoretically uncalibrated even if every member is calibrated (Ranjan and Gneiting 2010, Section 2). Pulled toward badly calibrated members when weights are equal.
method_table.formula: p = sum_i w_i p_i with w_i = 1/k
method_table.prerequisite-data: current member probabilities p_1..p_k only; no resolved verdicts
method_table.role: the method identified as usable at zero history

method_table.calibration_when_members_differ: Sharper than linear pooling; ML-weighted log-linear can be near-optimal on independent sources (Allard Table 4) once labels exist.
method_table.formula: p ∝ exp(sum_i w_i log p_i), w_i = 1/k, then binary-renormalized
method_table.prerequisite-data: current member probabilities p_1..p_k only, plus a floor/clipping convention for 0/1 reports; no resolved verdicts for equal weights. ML / calibrated log-linear weights additionally need a labelled (forecast, outcome) panel (Allard et al. 2012, Theorem 1).
method_table.why_not_the_zero_history_pick: Computationally defined at zero history, but not identified as the usable-today method: 0/1 forcing lets one overconfident miscalibrated member veto the pool, and the live unequal-calibration control scores it worse than equal-weight linear pooling.

method_table.calibration_when_members_differ: This is the operator designed for unequal skill: posterior mass concentrates on historically better-calibrated members. Live control seed 79: ECE 0.017802 versus equal-linear ECE 0.033567 after 400 labelled rows; Brier 0.207865 versus 0.209190.
method_table.formula: w_i = P(M_i | y_train) ∝ P(y_train | M_i) P(M_i); pooled forecast is the linear mixture of member densities with those weights (Raftery et al. 2005 eq. after the law of total probability)
method_table.prerequisite-data: a labelled training window of member forecasts AND verifying outcomes (Raftery et al. 2005 used 25 days of 48-h temperature forecasts and observations to hit 90.0% coverage of 90% intervals). Uniform prior plus empty history ⇒ w_i = 1/k, i.e. equal-weight linear pooling.
method_table.role: best calibrated of the three once labels exist; blocked today

method_table.calibration_when_members_differ: Down-weights historically poorly calibrated members. Not one of the three named pooling families; recorded because the call sheet grades it. Live ECE 0.027676 versus equal-linear 0.033567.
method_table.formula: w_i ∝ 1 / mean_t (p_{i,t} - y_t)^2, then linear pool
method_table.prerequisite-data: the same labelled (forecast, verdict) history the call sheet already grades as missing; blocked on an empty store

question: Between linear pooling, logarithmic pooling and Bayesian aggregation, which produces better calibrated group forecasts when members differ in calibration - and what does each require that this program does not yet have (a labelled verdict history)?

strongest_surviving_counterargument: Equal-weight logarithmic pooling is also computable at zero history, so naming linear pooling as the unique today-method is a robustness choice (0/1 forcing + worse live ECE/Brier on the unequal-calibration DGP), not a theorem that log pooling is undefined. If this program later prefers sharpness over veto-robustness and clips 0/1 reports, log pooling could be the zero-history operator. That does not unblock BMA.
